what: serving speed of the API (backlog item 13); not accuracy
caveat: the CI test bundle has untrained weights: these numbers measure serving speed only, never accuracy
where: Claude Code cloud session container (shared VM), 2026-11-09

software.torch_threads_note: read in the client process; the server uses the same default

server: scripts/bench_app.py: app/api/main.py's create_app, one uvicorn worker, rate limiter opened wide
conditions: client and server share the same machine's CPUs; every request opens a new connection (urllib sends Connection: close); the API runs each request in a worker thread, so concurrent requests compute in parallel and compete for the CPUs; CPU use is not measured
image: one synthetic 448x448 JPEG, sent repeatedly; 10 warm-up requests not counted

annotations_by_hand.note: written by Claude after the run, from the numbers above and the repo; not script output
annotations_by_hand.not_the_champion: the test bundle has 1 network; the champion runs 3 per image (the 3-seed ensemble), so its latency and throughput are not these numbers. Measuring it needs the champion bundle (a release asset the owner uploads, as for item 6).
annotations_by_hand.differs_from_the_api_image: this run used torch 2.15.0+cu132 (a CUDA build from PyPI, run on CPU), not the image's torch 2.14.0 CPU build, and no Docker container; memory in particular may differ from the image. .github/workflows/benchmark.yml measures on a GitHub runner with the CPU build.
annotations_by_hand.reading: throughput stays at about 44 to 53 images a second from 1 to 20 users while median latency grows from 18.4 ms to 458.6 ms, roughly in proportion to the users: the machine is saturated. The mechanism is not measured: concurrent requests compute in parallel worker threads (each with torch's default intra-op threads) and compete for the 4 CPUs with each other and with the client's threads. More processes with fewer threads each, or a lighter model, are the likely levers; not measured.
annotations_by_hand.unreconciled_with_phase_3: Phase 3's ONNX parity job measured PyTorch EfficientNet-B0 at a median of about 93 ms per seed for one already-preprocessed image on Databricks serverless (4 CPUs; results/phase3/onnx/results.json). Here a whole request (decode, preprocessing, one B0, Mahalanobis, HTTP) took about 18 ms median on a different machine and torch build. The gap (about 5x) is not explained; hardware, torch version and thread settings all differ, and neither run recorded enough to separate them.
